subtopics.title: The Field Concept and the Rules of Field Lines

questions.question: An electric field is defined as:
options: A region of space in which an electric charge experiences a force
The path followed by an electron
The charge stored on a sphere

questions.question: The direction of the electric field at a point is the direction of the force on:
options: A negative test charge at that point
A positive test charge at that point

questions.question: Which statement about field lines is FALSE?
options: Field lines may cross where two fields overlap
Field lines start on positive charge and end on negative charge
Closer lines mean a stronger field
Field lines around a negative point charge point inward

questions.question: Outside its surface, the field of a uniformly charged sphere looks like:
options: A uniform field of parallel lines
Two unlike point charges side by side
The field of a point charge located at the sphere's centre

subtopics.title: Field Strength from Force — E Equals F Over q

questions.question: Electric field strength is defined as:
options: The force per unit positive charge at a point
The total force a charge can produce
The energy stored at a point

questions.question: A +2 × 10⁻⁶ C charge at point P experiences a force of 0,008 N east. The field at P is:
If the test charge at a point is doubled, the field strength at that point:
options: Stays the same, because the force doubles as well

questions.question: An electron sits in a field that points east. The force on the electron is:
options: Zero, because electrons are too small
West, against the field, because its charge is negative

subtopics.title: Field of a Point Charge — E Equals k Q Over r Squared

questions.question: The electric field 0,3 m from a +5 μC point charge is:
options: 5 × 10⁵ N·C⁻¹, directed away from the charge

questions.question: In E = kQ/r², the charge Q is:
options: The test charge placed in the field
Always the smaller of the two charges
The source charge creating the field

questions.question: Doubling your distance from a point charge changes the field strength to:
You know the distance from a known source charge and want the field there. You should use:

subtopics.title: Fields from More Than One Charge

questions.question: The net field at a point due to several charges is found by:
options: Adding the field contributions as vectors, one per source charge
Adding all the source charges first and using one formula

questions.question: P lies midway between +2 μC at A and −3 μC at B. The two field contributions at P point:
options: Both from A toward B — away from the positive and toward the negative
At right angles to the line AB

questions.question: With contributions of 4,5 × 10⁵ and 6,75 × 10⁵ N·C⁻¹ in the same direction, the net field at P is:
Somewhere between two positive charges the net field is zero because:
options: Positive charges create no field between them
The field lines cross at that point
The two contributions point in opposite directions and cancel exactly there

subtopics.title: The Invisible Cushion Around Every Charge

questions.question: A charge exerts a force on another charge far away without touching it because:
options: The second charge feels the first charge's field at its own location
Air carries the force between them

questions.question: In a field-line diagram, the arrows show:
options: The direction a small positive test charge would be pushed
The direction of the strongest wind
The direction a negative charge would be pushed

questions.question: Field lines crowd close together near a charge because:
options: The diagram runs out of space
The field is strongest close to the charge
The charge pulls the lines inward

subtopics.title: How Hard Is the Shove at This Spot?

questions.question: Field strength is quoted as force PER COULOMB so that:
options: The number describes the location itself, independent of the test charge used

questions.question: The rand-per-kilogram comparison teaches that field strength is like:
options: The total on the till slip
A rate that lets you compare places fairly

questions.question: A spot rated 4 000 N·C⁻¹ delivers what force to a 2 × 10⁻⁶ C visitor?
An electron placed in a field reads the arrows on the map:
options: Correctly — it moves along the arrows
Not at all — fields ignore electrons
Sideways — it moves at right angles to the arrows
In reverse — it is shoved against the arrows

subtopics.title: When Two Charges Both Have a Say

questions.question: At a point between a positive charge on the left and a negative charge on the right, the two field contributions:
options: Point the same way and add, making the field strong

questions.question: Between two EQUAL positive charges, the net field is zero:
options: At the surface of each charge

questions.question: If the two charges are unequal and alike, the zero-field point sits:
options: Outside the pair, beyond the stronger charge

questions.question: A field can be calculated at an empty point in space because:
options: Empty space always contains stray electrons
The formula only works for empty points
The calculation is hypothetical and has no meaning
The field exists there whether or not a charge is present to feel it
